items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Ill be at yours in about 3 mins but look out for me
clues: short and practical, like a real quick text
items.explanation: Real people text in a hurry: missing apostrophes and half sentences are a good sign of a human.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: I walked an hour 2 c u! doesnt that show I care y wont u believe im serious?
clues: '2 c u' and 'y wont u' text-speak
items.explanation: Strong, messy feelings and text-speak like '2 c u' are typical of real people, not polished AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Okay. No no, just shining on. That was meant to be signing, but that sounds better.
clues: jokes about its own autocorrect typo
items.explanation: People laugh at their own typos. AI rarely makes a typo and then jokes about it.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Quite lor. But dun tell him wait he get complacent...
clues: refers to someone without explaining who
items.explanation: Local slang and references only the friend would understand are hard for AI to fake.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Garbage bags, eggs, jam, bread, hannaford wheat chex
items.explanation: A bare list with no greeting is how people really text family. AI tends to add friendly sentences around it.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Hmm...Bad news...Hype park plaza $700 studio taken...Only left 2 bedrm-$900...
items.explanation: Specific, slightly chaotic details (prices, a plaza name, lots of '...') point to a real person.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Printer is cool. I mean groovy. Wine is groovying
items.explanation: Odd little jokes that only make sense in the moment are very human.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Will it help if we propose going back again tomorrow
items.explanation: Some real messages are plain and tidy. When there are no clues, it's fine to be unsure.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Having lunch:)you are not in online?why?
items.explanation: Rushed punctuation like 'lunch:)you' is a human habit. AI writes neatly spaced sentences.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: It's fine, imma get a drink or somethin. Want me to come find you?
items.explanation: Casual slang and dropped letters are a sign of a real person typing fast.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Boo I'm on my way to my moms. She's making tortilla soup. Yummmm
items.explanation: Stretched words like 'Yummmm' are how people show feelings in texts.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Just finished eating. Got u a plate. NOT leftovers this time.
items.explanation: The capital 'NOT' points to a shared history only these two people know about.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: I shall book chez jules for half eight, if that's ok with you?
items.explanation: Polite and well written, but very specific plans like 'half eight' at a named place feel real.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Tee hee. Off to lecture, cheery bye bye.
items.explanation: Playful sign-offs like 'cheery bye bye' are personal quirks that AI doesn't usually copy.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Oh and by the way you do have more food in your fridge! Want to go out for a meal tonight?
clues: complete, friendly sentences with an exclamation mark
items.explanation: This one reads almost like AI because it's tidy, but it's real. Neat writing alone doesn't prove AI.

items.subject: prize
items.content: URGENT! Your Mobile number has been awarded a <UKP>2000 prize GUARANTEED. Call 09061790125 from landline. Claim 3030. Valid 12hrs only 150ppm
items.explanation: You can't win a prize you never entered. 'URGENT' plus 'call now' is a classic scam.

items.subject: prize
items.content: You have won a Nokia 7250i. This is what you get when you win our FREE auction. To take part send Nokia to 86021 now. HG/Suite342/2Lands Row/W1JHL 16+
clues: asks you to text a short code
items.explanation: Winning something you never took part in is a red flag. Texting short codes can cost money.

items.subject: phone-plan
items.content: 4mths half price Orange line rental & latest camera phones 4 FREE. Had your phone 11mths+? Call MobilesDirect free on 08000938767 to update now! or2stoptxt T&Cs
items.explanation: Unasked-for offers of free phones push you to call. Contact your provider through its official app instead.

items.subject: prize
items.content: Txt: CALL to No: 86888 & claim your reward of 3 hours talk time to use from your phone now! Subscribe6GBP/mnth inc 3hrs 16 stop?txtStop www.gamb.tv
clues: small print says you subscribe for 6GBP a month
items.explanation: Read the small print: 'Subscribe 6GBP/mnth' means the 'reward' costs you money every month.

items.subject: prize
items.content: Urgent! Please call 09061213237 from landline. £5000 cash or a luxury 4* Canary Islands Holiday await collection. T&Cs SAE PO Box 177. M227XY. 150ppm. 16+
items.explanation: Huge prizes and urgency are the oldest scam trick. Real companies don't hand out cash by text.

items.subject: phone-plan
items.content: December only! Had your mobile 11mths+? You are entitled to update to the latest colour camera mobile for Free! Call The Mobile Update Co FREE on 08002986906
items.explanation: Time pressure like 'December only!' is meant to stop you thinking. Check with your provider directly.

items.subject: prize
items.content: Ur balance is now £600. Next question: Complete the landmark, Big, A. Bob, B. Barry or C. Ben ?. Text A, B or C to 83738. Good luck!
items.explanation: A pretend balance and an easy quiz keep you texting a paid number. The money is never real.

items.subject: travel
items.content: "For the most sparkling shopping breaks from 45 per person; call 0121 2025050 or visit www.shortbreaks.org.uk"
items.explanation: Unsolicited deals pointing to unknown sites are spam. Search the company yourself before you call.

items.subject: landscape
clues: colours are extra bright, like a painting
items.explanation: Real forests have messy detail. Super bright, smooth colours often mean AI.

items.subject: landscape
items.explanation: Real landscapes are often a bit boring and messy. That ordinariness is a good sign.

items.subject: bird
clues: wires cross and tangle in a way that makes no sense
items.explanation: Follow lines like wires or cables. In AI images they often start and stop in random places.

items.subject: bird
clues: every bird has a slightly different pose
items.explanation: This looks almost too graphic, but each bird is unique and the wires sag like real ones.

items.subject: landscape
clues: trees look like blurry brush strokes up close
items.explanation: Distant towns and trees are often mush in AI images. Real photos keep some detail.

items.subject: landscape
clues: trees look soft in the mist
items.explanation: Mist can make a real photo look painted. Check the forest: individual trees stay sharp.

items.subject: animal
clues: the pink blob in the background has no clear shape
items.explanation: When the main subject looks perfect, check the background. Objects there often have no clear shape.

items.subject: animal
clues: natural fur, a slobbery toy, shallow background blur
items.explanation: Small real details like a chewed toy and individual hairs point to a real photo.

items.subject: animal
clues: the cage bars blend into the fur
the hand gripping the bar looks soft and melted
items.explanation: Look where two things touch, like a hand on a bar. AI often blurs or melts those edges.

items.subject: building
clues: straight, clean lines on the building
items.explanation: Straight lines that stay straight, and dull everyday weather, suggest a real photo.

items.subject: food
clues: the fruits melt into each other
some are half lime, half cucumber
items.explanation: AI mixes things together. Here the fruits blend into each other and don't look like one kind.

items.subject: food
clues: small bananas are each slightly different
items.explanation: Natural decay like torn, brown leaves is hard for AI to fake well.

items.subject: bird
clues: the bird's legs are very thin and stiff
items.explanation: Look at thin parts like legs and feet. AI often makes them too thin or not quite attached.

items.subject: bird
clues: small crow with a clear shape
items.explanation: A small, ordinary subject in a plain scene is typical of real photos.

items.subject: bird
items.explanation: Patterns like feathers or fabric often turn into random noise in AI images.

items.subject: animal
clues: a young deer half-hidden in leaves
items.explanation: Animals half hidden behind plants are hard for AI to draw convincingly.

items.subject: bird
clues: the shop shelves are made-up shapes
items.explanation: This is an illustration, not a photo. A cartoon style is the easiest clue.

items.subject: object
items.explanation: Studio product shots can look computer-made, but the tiny gears and fittings all make sense.

items.subject: building
clues: the roof lines go soft and wobbly
items.explanation: Black and white can hide AI mistakes. Zoom in on straight lines like roofs and fences.

items.subject: animal
clues: looks like a cartoon toy, not a real animal
items.explanation: Some AI images are not even trying to be photos. Shiny, toy-like animals are easy to spot.

items.subject: bird
clues: the ducks look like copies of each other
one duck is an odd yellow
items.explanation: When animals in a group look like clones, be suspicious. Real ducks all look a little different.

items.subject: bird
items.explanation: Real photos are often badly framed, with things in the way. AI usually makes a tidy picture.

items.subject: object
clues: the legs merge into the bench
items.explanation: Bodies are hard for AI: check where legs, hands or fingers meet other things.

items.subject: object
clues: odd split-toe shape and faded colour
items.explanation: These look strange, but they're real ancient socks in a museum. Weird doesn't always mean fake.

items.subject: landscape
clues: buildings on the shore melt into the water line
items.explanation: Sunsets are easy for AI. The only clue is the shoreline: the buildings don't have clear shapes.

items.subject: landscape
clues: ice and rocks with detailed texture
items.explanation: Look at the texture: real ice and rocks have lots of tiny, random detail.

items.subject: vehicle
clues: the wings and engines don't line up
items.explanation: AI often gets machines wrong. Count the wings, engines and wheels.

items.subject: vehicle
clues: a real old aircraft and a model figure
items.explanation: Complex structures like these beams stay consistent in real photos. AI usually tangles them.

items.subject: object
clues: heels and straps bend in impossible ways
items.explanation: Objects that float and twist into impossible shapes are a giveaway of AI.

items.subject: object
items.explanation: Lots of small objects that are all sharp and make sense usually means a real photo.

items.subject: landscape
clues: the sky is a smooth gradient and the sand has no tracks or texture
items.explanation: Very hard. Real deserts have footprints, stones and texture. Everything here is too clean.

items.subject: landscape
clues: cactus spines and rocks all different
items.explanation: Real nature is full of variety. No two cacti or rocks look the same.

items.subject: animal
items.explanation: Too-perfect, glowing eyes and painted-looking fur are common AI tells.

items.subject: animal
items.explanation: Readable text is a strong sign of a real photo. AI often writes gibberish.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Hey! Just wanted to check in and see how your day is going. Let me know if you'd like to grab dinner later this week — I'm free Thursday or Friday! 😊
clues: perfect punctuation and an em dash
items.explanation: AI texts often sound like a friendly template: tidy, upbeat and with no personal detail.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Good morning! I hope you slept well. Don't forget to drink plenty of water and take some time for yourself today. You've got this! 💪
items.explanation: Real friends rarely send a list of wellness tips. Motivational filler is a common AI habit.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Thanks so much for having us over last night! The food was absolutely delicious and we had such a wonderful time. Let's do it again soon!
items.explanation: Lots of praise but no details (which dish? what happened?) is a sign of AI writing.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Running a few minutes late, apologies for the inconvenience! I should be there in approximately 10 minutes.
clues: 'apologies for the inconvenience' and 'approximately' are too formal for a friend
items.explanation: Office-style phrases like 'apologies for the inconvenience' feel odd between friends.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Just picked up groceries! Got eggs, bread, milk, and some fresh veggies. Is there anything else you need while I'm out?
clues: a complete, tidy list with an Oxford comma
items.explanation: Compare it with a real shopping text: people just list items. AI wraps them in polite sentences.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Happy birthday!! 🎉 I hope your day is filled with joy, laughter, and everything that makes you smile. Can't wait to celebrate with you!
clues: card-style wish 'filled with joy, laughter, and...'
items.explanation: Birthday wishes in a neat list of three sound like a greeting card, a typical AI pattern.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that! That sounds really frustrating. Is there anything I can do to help? I'm here if you need to talk.
clues: says all the 'right' supportive things in order
items.explanation: AI is good at sounding caring in general, but it doesn't mention the actual problem.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: omg yes!! that movie was so good, the ending totally caught me off guard. we should def watch the sequel together
clues: uses casual style but still fully correct grammar
items.explanation: Even when AI writes casually, it often avoids naming specifics. Who forgets to say which film?

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Heading to the gym now, then I'll swing by the store. Want me to pick anything up for dinner?
items.explanation: This could easily be human. Tidy, complete plans are only a weak clue for AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: haha that's hilarious 😂 can't believe he actually said that to the teacher
clues: laughs at something without any detail
items.explanation: Hard one. Short reactions are easy for AI to imitate. Look for details only a real friend would know.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Sorry, I missed your call! Was in a meeting. Can I call you back in about 20 mins?
items.explanation: AI can write very normal messages. When nothing stands out, it's genuinely hard to tell.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: ugh traffic is awful today, stuck on the ring road. save me a seat?
items.explanation: AI can copy lowercase, casual texting. Be careful about trusting style alone.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Did you end up finding your keys? I swear they were on the kitchen counter this morning
items.explanation: Very hard: it refers to earlier events and leaves out the full stop, just like a person would.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: k see u at 7. bring the charger pls mine died
items.explanation: When AI is told to 'text like a person', it can be almost impossible to spot. That's why we check sources, not just style.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: mum says dinner's at 6 not 7, dont be late again lol
items.explanation: Even small 'human' mistakes can be generated. Don't rely on one clue; think about who is likely to send it.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: ParcelPost: Your package could not be delivered due to an unpaid fee of £1.99. Pay now to reschedule: parcel-track-help.info/pay
clues: link is not the real courier website
items.explanation: Couriers don't text you for small fees. Check deliveries in the official app or website.

items.subject: bank
items.content: SECURITY ALERT: A new device has signed in to your bank account. If this wasn't you, verify your identity immediately at secure-bank-verify.com
clues: urgent link to a look-alike website
items.explanation: Banks never ask you to 'verify' by clicking a link. Open your banking app yourself instead.

items.subject: family
items.content: Hi Mum, this is my new number, my phone broke. Can you save it and message me on WhatsApp? I need a small favour x
clues: unknown number claiming to be your child
items.explanation: Before helping, call your child on their OLD number or ask a question only they would know.

items.subject: tax
items.content: HMRC: You are eligible for a tax refund of £326.40. To claim, submit your details within 24 hours: gov-refund-claim.co
clues: tax office doesn't text refund links
items.explanation: Government tax offices don't send refund links by text. Real government sites end in .gov.uk.

items.subject: job
items.content: Hi! We saw your CV online. Earn £300-£500 a day working from home, just 1 hour needed. Reply YES to learn more.
items.explanation: If a job pays a lot for almost nothing and finds YOU, it's almost always a scam.

items.subject: account
items.content: Your streaming subscription has been paused because we couldn't process your payment. Update your billing info to avoid losing access: stream-billing-update.net
clues: link is not the service's real website
items.explanation: This looks routine, which makes it convincing. Always update payments inside the app, never through a text link.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Royal Mail: Your parcel is being held at our depot. A redelivery can be booked here: royalmail.redelivery-uk.com Ref: RM8842
items.explanation: Read links from right to left: this one belongs to 'redelivery-uk.com', not Royal Mail.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Your parcel from BookNook will be delivered today between 13:00 and 15:00. Track in the courier app. No action needed.
items.explanation: Real delivery updates just give information. Nothing to pay, nothing to click.

items.subject: appointment
items.content: Reminder: You have a dental appointment on Tuesday at 10:30 at Riverside Dental. Reply C to confirm or call the practice to change.
items.explanation: Reminders about something you booked yourself, with no links or payments, are normally safe.

items.subject: code
items.content: Your verification code is 482913. It expires in 10 minutes. Never share this code with anyone, including our staff.
clues: warns you never to share it
items.explanation: Genuine codes warn you not to share them. Only use one if YOU just asked for it.

items.subject: family
items.content: Hi love, landed safely! Bit tired. Will ring you tomorrow after work x
items.explanation: A message from a saved contact that asks for nothing is very unlikely to be a scam.

items.subject: bank
items.content: Bank: You spent £42.10 at GreenGrocer Market. If you don't recognise this, open your banking app or call the number on the back of your card.
clues: tells you to use your app or card number, not a link
items.explanation: Real banks send you to their app or the number on your card, never a link in the message.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: We missed you! Your parcel is at the Corner Shop collection point. Bring this code: 7XQ2. Collect within 7 days.
clues: 'missed you' sounds like scams, but no fee and no link
items.explanation: This looks like a scam at first, but there's no money and no link. Real updates just tell you where to go.

items.subject: account
items.content: Your password was changed. If this was you, you can ignore this message. If not, open the app and go to Settings > Security.
clues: security alert, but sends you to the app, not a link
items.explanation: Real security alerts tell you to open the app yourself. Scam versions give you a link.

items.subject: appointment
items.content: City Health: your flu vaccine is due. Book at reception or through your usual GP app. Reply STOP to opt out.
clues: official-sounding, but nothing to click or pay
items.explanation: Health reminders that send you to your usual GP app or reception are safe to act on.

items.subject: phone-plan
items.content: Your monthly bill of £18.00 is ready. It will be collected by Direct Debit on the 5th. View it any time in your account.
clues: bill reminder with no link and no pressure
items.explanation: Normal bills tell you the amount and when it will be paid. They don't threaten you or demand action now.

items.subject: bank
items.content: URGENT: We've blocked a payment of £900 on your card. Please call us on the number on the back of your card.
clues: says URGENT like a scam, but asks you to use the number on your own card
items.explanation: A tricky one: 'URGENT' feels scammy, but calling the number on your own card is exactly the safe thing to do.

items.subject: family
items.content: Hey it's Sam from the running club, got your number from the group list. Are you coming Saturday?
clues: unknown number, but explains where they got it
items.explanation: Unknown numbers aren't always scams. This one asks for nothing and you can check in the group chat.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Courier: Your driver Alex is 5 stops away. Live tracking is in the app. Leave-safe instructions can be updated there.
clues: first name of driver and 'live tracking' look like phishing bait, but no link
items.explanation: Real couriers do share driver names. The safe sign: it sends you to the app, not to a link.

items.subject: code
items.content: Someone tried to sign in to your account from a new device. If this was you, enter code 551904. If not, no action needed — your account is safe.
clues: looks like a scary alert, but nothing to click and no request
items.explanation: Very tricky: alerts can be real. The key is that it doesn't ask you to click, call or pay anything.

items.subject: tax
items.content: Council Tax: your annual bill is now available. Log in to your council account through your local council website to view it.
clues: mentions tax and bills, but no link and no deadline
items.explanation: Tax messages make people nervous. This one is fine because it tells you to go to the website yourself.

items.subject: appointment
items.content: Library: The book you reserved is ready to collect at Central Library. We'll keep it for 7 days.
items.explanation: Messages about something you asked for, with no link and no payment, are usually genuine.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Then ü wait 4 me at bus stop aft ur lect lar. If i dun c ü then i go get my car then come back n pick ü.
clues: 'ü', 'aft ur lect lar', 'dun c ü': heavy local text-speak
items.explanation: Heavy slang and shortcuts like 'dun c ü' are something AI almost never writes unless asked.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Yeah, don't go to bed, I'll be back before midnight
clues: a little bossy in a friendly way
items.explanation: Short, practical messages like this are typical of real people, but AI can write them too.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: I got lousy sleep. I kept waking up every 2 hours to see if my cat wanted to come in. I worry about him when its cold :(
items.explanation: A small, specific personal story (waking every 2 hours for the cat) points to a real person.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Just sent it. So what type of food do you like?
items.explanation: Nothing gives this one away. Plain messages are hard to judge, and that's normal.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Anyway i'm going shopping on my own now. Cos my sis not done yet. Dun disturb u liao.
items.explanation: Local slang words like 'liao' are a strong sign of a real person texting.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: And stop being an old man. You get to build snowman snow angels and snowball fights.
clues: playful teasing 'stop being an old man'
items.explanation: Teasing a friend directly feels human. AI messages tend to stay polite.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: From tomorrow onwards eve 6 to 3 work.
items.explanation: Real people write in shorthand that doesn't quite make sense to outsiders.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Or ill be a little closer like at the bus stop on the same street
items.explanation: Missing apostrophes and half-finished thoughts are human habits.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Sorry da..today i wont come to play..i have driving clas..
items.explanation: Typos and lots of '..' are things AI rarely does on its own.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.explanation: A wry little joke with an old-style smiley is very human.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: I keep ten rs in my shelf:) buy two egg.
clues: 'ten rs' (rupees) and broken grammar 'buy two egg'
items.explanation: Everyday errands written in broken grammar are a sign of a real person.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Ok . . now i am in bus. . If i come soon i will come otherwise tomorrow
items.explanation: Odd punctuation like '. .' is a personal habit that AI doesn't copy.

items.subject: sms-casual

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: We spend our days waiting for the ideal path to appear in front of us.. But what we forget is.. "paths are made by walking.. not by waiting.." Goodnight!
items.explanation: This looks like AI, but it's a real chain message people forwarded long before AI. Wise-sounding text isn't proof of AI.

items.subject: prize
items.content: WINNER! As a valued network customer you hvae been selected to receive a £900 reward! To collect call 09061701444. Valid 24 hours only. ACL03530150PM
items.explanation: Big rewards plus a short deadline is a classic scam. You can't win what you didn't enter.

items.subject: account
items.content: Please CALL 08712402779 immediately as there is an urgent message waiting for you
items.explanation: A vague 'urgent message' that only reveals itself if you call a paid number is a scam.

items.subject: prize
items.content: A £400 XMAS REWARD IS WAITING FOR YOU! Our computer has randomly picked you from our loyal mobile customers to receive a £400 reward. Just call 09066380611
items.explanation: Being 'randomly picked' for money is a scam. Real companies don't do this by text.

items.subject: account
items.content: <Forwarded from 21870000>Hi - this is your Mailbox Messaging SMS alert. You have 4 messages. You have 21 matches. Please call back on 09056242159 to retrieve your messages and matches
clues: looks like a voicemail alert, but asks you to call an 09 premium number
items.explanation: Fake voicemail alerts push you to call expensive numbers. Check voicemail the normal way on your phone.

items.explanation: Too smooth and too perfect: plastic-looking surfaces, glossy colours and studio light everywhere are common signs of AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Hi there! I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to let you know that I will be arriving at approximately 6:00 PM this evening. Looking forward to seeing you!
clues: 'I hope this message finds you well' is email language
items.explanation: Nobody texts a friend like a business email. Formal phrases are a big AI tell.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: What a wonderful day it has been! The weather was absolutely perfect for our picnic, and I'm so grateful we got to spend it together. Let's make more memories like this soon! ☀️🧺
items.explanation: Gushing, greeting-card language with neat emoji at the end is typical of AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Just a quick reminder that the book club meeting is tomorrow at 7 PM. Please bring your copy and any thoughts you'd like to share. See you there!
clues: sounds like a group announcement, very complete
items.explanation: Real friends rarely spell everything out this neatly. It reads like a notice, not a text.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Hey! I just tried that new café on the corner and it was amazing. The coffee was rich and smooth, and the pastries were so fresh. You definitely have to check it out!
items.explanation: Descriptions that sound like a review, but name nothing, are a sign of AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: No worries at all! Take your time, there's absolutely no rush. Just let me know whenever you're ready and we can figure out the details then.
items.explanation: AI tends to over-reassure ('no worries', 'no rush', 'whenever'). Real people say it once.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: lol I totally forgot about that! thanks for reminding me, I'll grab it on my way home
clues: casual but every word spelled correctly
items.explanation: Casual tone with perfect spelling, and no clue what 'it' is, can point to AI.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Can't make it tonight unfortunately, something came up at work. Rain check for next week?
items.explanation: This could easily be a real person. Neat, polite cancellations are a weak AI clue.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: omw! traffic's not too bad so should be there in 15ish
items.explanation: AI can copy text-speak like 'omw' when asked. Style alone can fool you.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: did u see the match last night?? cant believe that last minute goal
clues: missing apostrophe and double '??' look human
items.explanation: Looks human, but notice it never says which match or team. AI often stays vague.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: my mum's asking if you want the leftover lasagne, she made way too much again haha
clues: family detail and 'again haha' feel real
items.explanation: Small family details are easy for AI to invent. A believable story isn't proof.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: running late sorry!! bus just didn't show up. 10 mins
items.explanation: Very hard: rushed messages are easy to imitate. When in doubt, think about who would really send it.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: u still got my charger? need it back before thurs x
items.explanation: When AI is told to text casually, it can look exactly like a person. That's why we check who sent it, not just how it's written.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: ok so the shop was out of the oat milk, got the almond one instead hope thats fine
clues: everyday detail, missing apostrophe, no punctuation at the end
items.explanation: Even small 'mistakes' can be generated on purpose. There may be no visible clue at all.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: gonna be at the pub from 8, come by if ur free
items.explanation: Some AI messages are impossible to tell apart. That's an important lesson: don't trust a message just because it 'sounds human'.

items.subject: sms-casual
items.content: Ahh thank you!! Honestly needed that today. Coffee on me next time
clues: capital letters and tidy grammar but natural
items.explanation: Nothing here gives it away. Being unsure is the right answer sometimes.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: DHL Express: Customs duty of £2.49 is due for your parcel GB4471. Pay within 48h or it will be returned: dhl-customs-pay.com
items.explanation: Small fees are used so you don't think twice. Couriers' real sites are their own domains, not 'dhl-customs-pay.com'.

items.subject: account
items.content: Netflix: We're having trouble with your current billing information. Please update your details to keep watching: netflix-account-help.net
items.explanation: Using a real brand makes scams believable. Always update payments inside the app you already use.

items.subject: family
items.content: Dad it's me, I'm using a friend's phone, mine fell in the river 😩 Can you send £180 for a new one? I'll pay you back Friday. Don't call, can't talk right now
items.explanation: 'Don't call me' is the big red flag. A real child would be happy for you to call their friend's phone.

items.subject: bank
items.content: Lloyds Bank: Did you attempt a payment of £1,240.00 to M. Patel? If NOT, call our fraud team immediately on 020 7946 0018.
clues: real bank name and fraud wording
but gives its OWN number to call
items.explanation: Scammers include a phone number so you call them. Only call the number on the back of your card.

items.subject: tax
items.content: GOV.UK: Our records show you overpaid tax in 2025. You are due a refund of £214.80. Claim online before 30/10: gov-uk-taxrefund.com
items.explanation: Real government sites end in '.gov.uk'. 'gov-uk-taxrefund.com' is a different website.

items.subject: job
items.content: Hi, I'm Laura from a recruitment agency. Your profile matches a part-time remote role (£120-£350/day). Can I message you on WhatsApp with details?
items.explanation: Job scams start friendly and move you to WhatsApp. Real recruiters don't promise big daily pay for unknown roles.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Evri: We tried to deliver your parcel today but no one was home. Choose a new delivery slot: evri.redeliver-parcel.com
items.explanation: Read the link backwards: the real website is the last part before '.com'. Here that's 'redeliver-parcel', not Evri.

items.subject: account
items.content: Apple: Your Apple ID was used to sign in on a new iPhone near Manchester. If this wasn't you, lock your account here: apple-id-support-centre.com
items.explanation: Real security alerts ask you to open Settings yourself. Never follow a link in a security text.

items.subject: bank
items.content: Your card ending 4821 has been temporarily frozen due to unusual activity. To unfreeze, reply with your date of birth and postcode.
clues: no link at all, but asks for personal details by text
items.explanation: Banks never ask for your details by text reply. Personal info can be used to steal your identity.

items.subject: shopping
items.content: Amazon: Your order #204-5541 for Apple AirPods Pro (£229.00) has been confirmed. If you did not place this order, call 0808 157 0192 to cancel.
clues: an order you didn't make, designed to scare you into calling
items.explanation: Fake 'order confirmations' make you panic and call. Check your orders in the real app instead.

items.subject: appointment
items.content: Hi, this is Greenfield Vets. Biscuit is due her annual booster. Call us on the usual number or book online to arrange.
items.explanation: A reminder that knows your pet and asks nothing is almost certainly real.

items.subject: shopping
items.content: Thanks for shopping at Hilltop Hardware. Your receipt is in the app. Questions? Pop in or call the store.
items.explanation: Receipts for something you just bought, that ask for nothing, are normal.

items.subject: family
items.content: Mum, train's delayed 20 mins, don't wait for me for dinner. Love you
items.explanation: Messages from saved family numbers that ask for nothing are safe.

items.subject: code
items.content: Your Uber code: 7741. Never share this code. Didn't request it? You can ignore this message.
clues: a code you just asked for
items.explanation: Genuine login codes always say 'never share'. Only use one you requested yourself.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Your parcel was delivered at 14:12 and left in your safe place (porch). Photo in the app.
clues: delivery confirmation with no link or fee
items.explanation: A confirmation that just tells you what happened, with no link, is a normal update.

items.subject: travel
items.content: TrainLine: Your 08:45 to Leeds is running about 15 minutes late. We're sorry for the delay.
items.explanation: Travel updates for a journey you booked, with nothing to click, are genuine.

items.subject: account
items.content: You've signed in to Spotify on a new device: Chrome on Windows. If this wasn't you, go to your account settings to change your password.
clues: security alert, but no link, points to settings
items.explanation: Security alerts can be real. The safe ones send you to settings yourself, not to a link.

items.subject: bank
items.content: Barclays: You've set up a new payee 'J SMITH'. If you didn't do this, call us on the number on the back of your card.
clues: real bank name and a payee warning, but tells you to use your card's number
items.explanation: Looks scary, but it's the right advice: use the number on your card, not one in a text.

items.subject: delivery
items.content: Royal Mail: We have a parcel for you with £3.10 to pay. A grey card has been left at your address with how to pay.
clues: mentions a fee (scam-like), but points to a card at your door, not a link
items.explanation: Some real deliveries do have fees. The safe sign is that it doesn't ask you to pay through a link.

items.subject: job
items.content: Hi, it's Priya from BrightPath Recruitment, we spoke on Tuesday. The interview with Northside Ltd is confirmed for Mon 10am. I'll email the details.
clues: refers to a conversation you had
items.explanation: This sounds like a job scam at first, but it follows up on a real conversation and asks for nothing.

items.subject: tax
items.content: HMRC: Your tax return for 2025-26 is due by 31 January. Sign in to your account at gov.uk to complete it.
clues: a tax text without a link, pointing to gov.uk
items.explanation: Tricky: tax texts feel scammy, but this one only tells you to visit gov.uk yourself.

items.subject: bank
items.content: Monzo: Your card ending 7731 was declined at FreshMart because it's frozen. Unfreeze it in the app if this was you.
clues: card warning, but sends you to the app, asks for nothing
items.explanation: Very hard: card warnings look like scams, but this one only tells you to use your own app.

items.subject: code
items.content: Your WhatsApp code: 312-889. Don't share this code with others.
clues: looks like the codes scammers ask for
items.explanation: Codes are real when YOU asked for one. Scammers ask you to forward codes, so never send them on.

items.subject: family
items.content: Hi it's Tom's new number! Old phone finally died. Save this one 👍
clues: unknown 'new number' (a scam trick), but asks for nothing
items.explanation: This looks like the 'Hi Mum' scam, but it asks for nothing. Check by calling the old number before you save it.

items.subject: appointment
items.content: NHS: Your appointment at St Mary's Outpatients is on 4 Nov at 09:20. To cancel or change, call the number on your letter.
items.explanation: Health appointment texts are real when they match a letter you have and contain no links.
